error_findings: Obligation ownership is false: the only slice ("Contract") has purpose "Package the canonical Execution Planning contract" with boundary "Contract template, schema registration, and generated assets" and completion signal "The inert contract ships". It cannot deliver accepted behavior, migration, rollout, rollback, documentation, or affected-surface work, yet all six obligations are mapped to it. The plan can be fully executed (contract bytes match) while the accepted user-facing outcome is entirely undelivered.

Delivery Checklist obligations are generic placeholders: all eleven items read "Complete the standard delivery work." None restates an accepted behavior, migration, rollout, rollback, or documentation obligation, so the checklist does not cover the accepted scenario "Users receive reviewed execution outcomes" and leaves behavior for the implementer to invent.

Proof coverage is non-discriminating: the slice's only proof obligation is data-compatibility (`bun run test:schema-compatibility`). Items 1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,11 require behavior-boundary, plan-integrity, failure-signals, security-boundary, rollout-rollback, and documentation-contract, but no slice step invokes any of them. Every named slice check can pass while the accepted claim is false.

Slice tasks are not startable for the accepted work: the RED step (`bun run test:schema-compatibility` with the generated-contract fixture, expecting `canonical contract bytes differ`) is not the highest-risk accepted behavior. No step names a fixture, command, edit action, or real actor boundary for authorization, rollout, rollback, or documentation work.

Checklist item-4 (testing, "Prove Accepted behavior at the named boundary.") is recorded with an empty Required proof and reviewed_disposition not_applicable with the reason "No runtime proof is needed." The accepted Implementation Plan states under Accepted proof boundaries: "Accepted behavior must be proven through behavior-boundary; this is applicable contributor work." Only optional categories explicitly recorded as inapplicable by the accepted Implementation Plan may be dispositioned not_applicable. As written, the checklist can be fully satisfied while the accepted testing obligation is never exercised, and the plan would report completion while the accepted user-facing proof claim is false. Restore item-4 as an open contributor obligation with required_proof behavior-boundary (a real_boundary, current_required proof already in the table).

execution-plan.md Measurement execution: the completion signal states "p95 authorization latency at or below 300 milliseconds", but implementation-plan.md's accepted measurement contract sets the target at "p95 authorization latency is at most 200 milliseconds over a rolling seven-day window". The plan simultaneously claims "the accepted outcome, population, target, ... remain unchanged", so delivery could report the measurement obligation satisfied at 250 ms while the accepted target is violated. Measurement execution changes the accepted measurement origin. Implementation Plan: 'record the duration at the gateway authorization boundary before response serialization.' Execution Plan instrumentation: 'record the duration in the client after response parsing.' Client-side post-parse timing includes network and serialization time, so the p95 <=200ms target measures a different quantity and could pass or fail independently of the accepted contract. Measurement execution contradicts the accepted validity safeguard. execution-plan.md 'Measurement execution' → Tests states the instrumentation tests 'accept evidence at any sample coverage', while implementation-plan.md 'Validity safeguards' requires rejecting evidence when sample coverage is below 99 percent. As written, a run with 40 percent coverage would pass the named tests and could be reported as satisfying the p95 target, so the accepted measurement claim can be falsely reported as met. The plan simultaneously asserts 'Preserved contract: ... validity safeguards ... remain unchanged', which is untrue, and its completion signal still demands 99 percent coverage — two reasonable implementations are permitted and one violates the accepted contract.

The supplied proof for the measurement obligation is non-discriminating with respect to the safeguard. No proof specification exercises sample-coverage rejection, and the tests as described explicitly tolerate any coverage, so the safeguard can be broken while every named proof command (including plan-integrity) still passes.

execution-plan.md, Measurement execution > Failure handling: "continue rollout and treat missing samples as a passing measurement" contradicts the accepted Failure behavior in implementation-plan.md ("keep rollout disabled and report the measurement as invalid when a validity safeguard fails").
